query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A multiscale simulation framework that incorporates bespoke interatomic potentials tuned to capture the local chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) will more accurately predict exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity compared with traditional ab initio or empirical methods. This is because the tailored potentials explicitly account for disorder‐enhanced phonon scattering, a critical mechanism in these materials, resulting in a quantitative improvement in prediction accuracy.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or near-equimolar high-entropy alloys in a disordered solid-solution state, typical for thermal-insulation applications.
generation.intervention: Application of a new computational predictive approach based on a multiscale simulation framework with bespoke interatomic potentials.
generation.conditions: Measurements performed in the temperature regime (e.g., room temperature to moderately high temperatures) where phonon conduction is the dominant heat transfer mechanism.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder that enhance phonon scattering.
generation.mechanism: The approach works by explicitly incorporating the effect of local chemical disorder into the description of interatomic forces, leading to enhanced phonon scattering. This more accurately reflects the intrinsic disorder-induced vibrational dynamics in HEAs, resulting in a lower phonon thermal conductivity than predicted by models that neglect such detailed atomic-scale heterogeneity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The new predictive method will yield measurements of phonon thermal conductivity with a significantly reduced error margin (tentatively, an improvement on the order of 10-20% lower prediction error) compared to current prediction models.
generation.baseline: Traditional prediction methods (e.g., standard ab initio calculations or semi-empirical models) that do not fully incorporate the effects of chemical disorder are expected to have higher errors or overestimate the conductivity.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies primarily to HEAs with pronounced chemical disorder (e.g., equimolar or near-equimolar compositions) in thermal-insulating conditions where phonon conduction dominates. It may not be applicable for HEAs or other alloys where alternative heat transfer mechanisms prevail, or where local disorder is minimal.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty in the exact magnitude of the predicted improvement and its universality across all HEA compositions. Additionally, the limits may be affected by temperature-dependent anharmonic effects that are not fully captured in the current framework.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a series of equimolar or near-equimolar HEAs predicted to have low phonon thermal conductivity by the new approach, and a comparable set evaluated via traditional prediction methods. Synthesize these alloys and measure their phonon thermal conductivity using time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) or a similar high-precision technique over the relevant temperature range. Compare the measured thermal conductivities against the predictions from both methods.
measurements: Phonon thermal conductivity values as a function of temperature
Quantitative error margins between predicted and experimental values for both approaches
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the new predictive method does not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction (e.g., less than a 10% improvement in prediction error compared to traditional models) in the discrepancy between prediction and experiment, then the hypothesis—that the multiscale simulation framework with bespoke potentials yields superior predictions—will be falsified.

These advanced systems are often required to operate under harsh conditions to optimize efficiency, which poses several challenges for the available materials. An example of advanced power system is one that is associated with fusion energy [1] . Beyond traditional fission-based systems, fusion reactors not only promise nearly unlimited clean energy, but also avoid the generation of long-life radioactive waste produced in fission devices. The CALPHAD approach [38] – [40] is currently the only method that can be used to obtain multicomponent phase diagrams with enough accuracy for practical applications without the need of the heavy experimental work [41] . This argument has made the CALPHAD method a key building block in the two largest driving forces in materials engineering today—ICME (Integrated computational materials engineering) [42] and MGI (Materials Genome Initiative) [43] . The application of the CALPHAD method requires both the thermodynamic database to provide the Gibbs energies (as a function of pressure, temperature, and composition) for the individual phases and the computational software to calculate the equilibrium state by an energy-minimization procedure. frame.system: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) engineered for thermal-insulation applications, characterized by complex, disordered multi-element microstructures that enhance phonon scattering.
frame.goal: To develop and validate a predictive approach capable of accurately identifying HEAs with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity, thereby outperforming current prediction methods.
frame.limitation: The current challenge lies in the unspecified nature of the predictive approach—its theoretical foundation, reliability across different HEA compositions, and defined applicability limits remain unestablished.
constraints: must explain why the approach is theoretically sound (e.g., based on emerging scattering mechanisms or novel computational descriptors)
must quantitatively predict improvement over existing prediction models
must define limits of applicability across HEA compositions and microstructures
should identify supportive evidence from either computational benchmarks or preliminary experiments
must specify a decisive experimental benchmark along with a clear outcome (e.g., a threshold thermal conductivity value) that would falsify the hypothesis
frame.regime: Operating conditions relevant to thermal insulation, likely spanning room temperature to moderately high temperatures where phonon conduction is the dominant heat transfer mechanism in HEAs.
prior_attempts: Traditional methods such as ab initio calculations, empirical models, and simplified phonon scattering theories which have not adequately captured the complex vibrational dynamics in multi-component disordered systems.

families.principle: Develop advanced computational frameworks with novel interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate the effects of chemical disorder and complex phonon scattering mechanisms in HEAs.
cues_for: explain why the approach would work
cues_against: traditional methods such as ab initio calculations and empirical models have been attempted but failed to fully capture the complex vibrational dynamics
families.best_lever: A multi–scale simulation framework that uses bespoke interatomic potentials tuned to reproduce disorder‐enhanced phonon scattering, thereby enabling predictions of low thermal conductivity in HEAs.

potential to leverage emerging computational descriptors and scattering mechanisms
cues_against: reliance on data quality and potential extrapolation issues across the vast compositional space of HEAs
families.best_lever: Developing a physics-informed ML model that incorporates vibrational density-of-states and local disorder metrics, trained on a curated dataset combining simulation and experimental results.

families.principle: Employ enhanced sampling techniques to better capture the configurational space and the free energy landscape associated with disordered HEAs, which can influence anharmonic phonon dynamics.
cues_for: novel computational descriptors that could capture subtle vibrational phenomena
cues_against: the central goal is prediction of thermal conductivity rather than solely mapping free energy landscapes; current emphasis is not on statistical sampling alone
families.best_lever: Using advanced Monte Carlo or molecular dynamics sampling methods to resolve low-energy vibrational states in HEAs that are directly linked to phonon scattering rates.

families.principle: Develop a decisive experimental technique that directly measures phonon thermal conductivity and microstructural features in HEAs to validate predictive models.
cues_for: clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis
cues_against: the focus is on a predictive (theoretical/computational) approach, whereas measurement methods serve primarily to benchmark and falsify predictions
families.best_lever: Implementing high-precision time-domain thermoreflectance measurements that can resolve subtle differences in phonon scattering owed to compositional disorder.
